claim: Histone sumoylation has been associated with gene regulation, centromeric localization, and double-strand break repair in eukaryotes.
source: The post-translational modification of histones by the small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) protein has been associated with gene regulation, centromeric localization, and double-strand break repair in eukaryotes.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature establishing these associations.

claim: Sumoylation of histone H4 was specifically associated with gene repression.
source: Although sumoylation of histone H4 was specifically associated with gene repression, this could not be proven due to the challenge of site-specifically sumoylating H4 in cells.
evidence: This claim references prior associations from the literature but notes they were not definitively proven.

claim: H4K12su inhibits transcription-activating H4 tail acetylation by p300 in mononucleosomes.
source: Mononucleosome-based assays revealed that H4K12su inhibits transcription-activating H4 tail acetylation by the histone acetyltransferase p300, as well as transcription-associated H3K4 methylation by the extended catalytic module of the Set1/COMPASS (complex of proteins associated with Set1) histone methyltransferase complex.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from mononucleosome-based assays described in the manuscript.

claim: H4K12su inhibits transcription-associated H3K4 methylation by the extended catalytic module of Set1/COMPASS.
source: Mononucleosome-based assays revealed that H4K12su inhibits transcription-activating H4 tail acetylation by the histone acetyltransferase p300, as well as transcription-associated H3K4 methylation by the extended catalytic module of the Set1/COMPASS (complex of proteins associated with Set1) histone methyltransferase complex.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from mononucleosome-based assays described in the manuscript.

claim: H4K12su inhibits both H4 tail acetylation and RNA polymerase II-mediated transcription in activator- and p300-dependent in vitro transcription assays with chromatinized plasmids.
source: Activator- and p300-dependent in vitro transcription assays with chromatinized plasmids revealed that H4K12su inhibits both H4 tail acetylation and RNA polymerase II-mediated transcription.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from in vitro transcription assays described in the manuscript.

claim: Cell-based assays with a SUMO-H4 fusion that mimics H4 tail sumoylation confirmed the negative crosstalk between histone sumoylation and acetylation/methylation.
source: Finally, cell-based assays with a SUMO-H4 fusion that mimics H4 tail sumoylation confirmed the negative crosstalk between histone sumoylation and acetylation/methylation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from cell-based assays described in the manuscript.

claim: Histone sumoylation plays a key role in gene silencing.
source: Thus, our studies establish the key role for histone sumoylation in gene silencing and its negative biochemical crosstalk with active transcription-associated marks in human cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Histone sumoylation engages in negative biochemical crosstalk with active transcription-associated marks in human cells.
source: Thus, our studies establish the key role for histone sumoylation in gene silencing and its negative biochemical crosstalk with active transcription-associated marks in human cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Histone sumoylation was first reported in human HEK293T and P493-6 B cells by Shiio and Eisenman, 2003.
source: First reported in human HEK293T and P493-6 B cells by Shiio and Eisenman, 2003, histone sumoylation also occurs in yeast (Ryu et al., 2019), parasitic protozoans (Issar et al., 2008), and plants (Miller et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the work of Shiio and Eisenman, 2003.

claim: Histone sumoylation occurs in yeast.
source: First reported in human HEK293T and P493-6 B cells by Shiio and Eisenman, 2003, histone sumoylation also occurs in yeast (Ryu et al., 2019), parasitic protozoans (Issar et al., 2008), and plants (Miller et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Ryu et al., 2019.

claim: Histone sumoylation occurs in parasitic protozoans.
source: First reported in human HEK293T and P493-6 B cells by Shiio and Eisenman, 2003, histone sumoylation also occurs in yeast (Ryu et al., 2019), parasitic protozoans (Issar et al., 2008), and plants (Miller et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Issar et al., 2008.

claim: Histone sumoylation occurs in plants.
source: First reported in human HEK293T and P493-6 B cells by Shiio and Eisenman, 2003, histone sumoylation also occurs in yeast (Ryu et al., 2019), parasitic protozoans (Issar et al., 2008), and plants (Miller et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Miller et al., 2010.

claim: Sumoylation occurs on all core histones, the linker histone H1, the histone variants H2A.Z and H2A.X, and the centromeric histone variant Cse4 in yeast.
source: Similar to histone ubiquitylation, sumoylation occurs on all core histones, the linker histone H1, the histone variants H2A.Z and H2A.X, and the centromeric histone variant Cse4 in yeast (Hendriks and Vertegaal, 2016; Ohkuni et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hendriks and Vertegaal, 2016 and Ohkuni et al., 2016.

claim: K12 in histone H4 is a major recurring site of sumoylation by SUMO-2/3.
source: Pioneering efforts to identify specific lysine sites of sumoylation identified K12 in histone H4 as a major recurring site of sumoylation by SUMO-2/3 (H4K12su) (Galisson et al., 2011; Hendriks et al., 2014), although multiple proximal lysines in the H4 N-terminal tail may also be enzymatically sumoylated in vitro (Hendriks and Vertegaal, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Galisson et al., 2011 and Hendriks et al., 2014.

claim: Multiple proximal lysines in the H4 N-terminal tail may be enzymatically sumoylated in vitro.
source: Pioneering efforts to identify specific lysine sites of sumoylation identified K12 in histone H4 as a major recurring site of sumoylation by SUMO-2/3 (H4K12su) (Galisson et al., 2011; Hendriks et al., 2014), although multiple proximal lysines in the H4 N-terminal tail may also be enzymatically sumoylated in vitro (Hendriks and Vertegaal, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hendriks and Vertegaal, 2016.

claim: Genetic studies in yeast and human cells have typically associated H4 sumoylation with the repression of gene transcription.
source: Genetic studies in yeast and human cells have typically associated H4 sumoylation with the repression of gene transcription, although mechanistic studies of the direct roles for histone sumoylation in human cells have remained intractable due to the dynamic nature and low abundance of sumoylation (Shiio and Eisenman, 2003; Nathan et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Shiio and Eisenman, 2003 and Nathan et al., 2006.

claim: H4K12su is incompatible with the compact chromatin structures seen in transcriptionally silent heterochromatin.
source: Biophysical studies of chromatin-array compaction remarkably showed that H4K12su is incompatible with the compact chromatin structures seen in transcriptionally silent heterochromatin.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior biophysical studies referenced in the manuscript.

claim: H4K12su stimulates intranucleosomal activity of the H3K4me2-specific histone demethylase LSD1.
source: Subsequent biochemical studies revealed that H4K12su stimulates intranucleosomal activity of the H3K4me2-specific histone demethylase LSD1 (Dhall et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dhall et al., 2017.

claim: Acetylation of lysine side-chains on H3 and H4 by p300 is necessary for efficient activator-driven transcription of 11 nm chromatin.
source: One such modification, acetylation of lysine side-chains on H3 and H4 by the acetyltransferase p300, is necessary for efficient activator-driven transcription of both 11 nm chromatin (An et al., 2002) and 30 nm linker histone H1-containing heterochromatin, likely through mechanisms that include direct decompaction of chromatin upon H4K16 acetylation and octamer eviction by the chromatin remodeler NAP1 (Robinson et al., 2008; Shimada et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to An et al., 2002.

claim: Acetylation of lysine side-chains on H3 and H4 by p300 is necessary for efficient activator-driven transcription of 30 nm linker histone H1-containing heterochromatin.
source: One such modification, acetylation of lysine side-chains on H3 and H4 by the acetyltransferase p300, is necessary for efficient activator-driven transcription of both 11 nm chromatin (An et al., 2002) and 30 nm linker histone H1-containing heterochromatin, likely through mechanisms that include direct decompaction of chromatin upon H4K16 acetylation and octamer eviction by the chromatin remodeler NAP1 (Robinson et al., 2008; Shimada et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Robinson et al., 2008 and Shimada et al., 2019.

claim: Site-specifically sumoylated human histone H4 at Lys12 (H4K12su) was obtained by a semisynthetic strategy using the ligation auxiliary 2-aminooxyethanethiol.
source: Site-specifically sumoylated human histone H4 at Lys12, H4K12su, was obtained by a semisynthetic strategy using the ligation auxiliary 2-aminooxyethanethiol (Figure 1A and B; Dhall et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental methods described and shown in Figure 1A and B, with citation to Dhall et al., 2017.

claim: The semisynthetic sumoylated H4 was incorporated into octamers with purified recombinant human histones H2A, H2B, and H3.
source: The semisynthetic sumoylated H4 was incorporated into octamers with purified recombinant human histones H2A, H2B, and H3 (Figure 1C and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Nucleosomes were reconstituted from sumoylated octamers using the 147 bp Widom 601 double-stranded DNA.
source: Nucleosomes were reconstituted from sumoylated octamers using the 147 bp Widom 601 double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: H4 from octamers containing H4K12su was devoid of acetylation, including H4K16ac.
source: Strikingly, H4 from octamers containing H4K12su was devoid of acetylation, including H4K16ac (Figure 1E bottom panel), which is strongly associated with chromatin decompaction and active gene transcription (Robinson et al., 2008; Akhtar and Becker, 2000; Shogren-Knaak et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E and citations to prior literature.

claim: H4K16ac is strongly associated with chromatin decompaction and active gene transcription.
source: Strikingly, H4 from octamers containing H4K12su was devoid of acetylation, including H4K16ac (Figure 1E bottom panel), which is strongly associated with chromatin decompaction and active gene transcription (Robinson et al., 2008; Akhtar and Becker, 2000; Shogren-Knaak et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Robinson et al., 2008, Akhtar and Becker, 2000, and Shogren-Knaak et al., 2006.

claim: The inhibition of H4 tail acetylation does not arise from allosteric inactivation of p300.
source: Importantly, the inhibition of H4 tail acetylation does not arise from allosteric inactivation of p300, deduced from our observation that H2A/H2B/H3 in H4K12su octamers were acetylated to the same extent as in wt H4 octamers.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations and logical inference from the data.

claim: H2A/H2B/H3 in H4K12su octamers were acetylated to the same extent as in wt H4 octamers.
source: Importantly, the inhibition of H4 tail acetylation does not arise from allosteric inactivation of p300, deduced from our observation that H2A/H2B/H3 in H4K12su octamers were acetylated to the same extent as in wt H4 octamers.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations.

claim: SUMO-3 did not inhibit p300 autoacetylation.
source: Additionally, western blots confirmed that SUMO-3 did not inhibit p300 autoacetylation, which is associated with robust acetyltransferase activity (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: p300 autoacetylation is associated with robust acetyltransferase activity.
source: Additionally, western blots confirmed that SUMO-3 did not inhibit p300 autoacetylation, which is associated with robust acetyltransferase activity (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge in the field.

claim: The inhibition of H4 acetylation in H4K12su is likely due to lysine acetylation site occlusion by proximal SUMO-3 in the H4 tail.
source: Hence the inhibition of H4 acetylation in H4K12su is likely due to lysine acetylation site occlusion by proximal SUMO-3 in the H4 tail.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental observations.

claim: H4 acetylation was suppressed in mononucleosomes containing H4K12su, but not in unmodified H4 mononucleosomes.
source: H4 acetylation was also suppressed in mononucleosomes containing H4K12su, but not in unmodified H4 mononucleosomes (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: SUMO-3 in the H4 tail is inhibitory toward p300-mediated acetylation of chromatin.
source: Our results unequivocally suggested that SUMO-3 in the H4 tail is inhibitory toward p300-mediated acetylation of chromatin, a process that is necessary for active gene transcription.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: p300-mediated acetylation of chromatin is necessary for active gene transcription.
source: Our results unequivocally suggested that SUMO-3 in the H4 tail is inhibitory toward p300-mediated acetylation of chromatin, a process that is necessary for active gene transcription.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge in the field.

claim: The presence of DNA inhibits p300 activity to a similar extent as observed with mononucleosomes.
source: The presence of DNA was sufficient to inhibit p300 activity to a similar extent as observed with mononucleosomes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Additional factors, such as transcription factor and RNAPII binding, enable robust p300 activity on histones during transcription initiation and elongation.
source: This unexpected inhibition of p300 activity by free DNA suggests that additional factors, such as transcription factor and RNAPII binding, enable robust p300 activity on histones during transcription initiation and elongation.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental observations.

claim: H4K12su does not inhibit the formation of recombinant chromatin.
source: Limited micrococcal nuclease (MNase) digestion of the transcription templates revealed the periodic spacing of nucleosomes in chromatin assembled with either wt H4 or H4K12su octamers, and clearly indicated that H4K12su does not inhibit the formation of recombinant chromatin (Figure 2B and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Transcription from templates assembled with H4K12su was drastically inhibited when compared with templates assembled with wt H4.
source: Surprisingly, and in contrast to the direct structural decompaction of chromatin by H4K12su, transcription from templates assembled with H4K12su was drastically inhibited when compared with templates assembled with wt H4.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from in vitro transcription assays.

claim: The addition of trichostatin A did not lead to significant changes in transcription from chromatinized templates assembled with H4K12su.
source: The addition of trichostatin A, a nanomolar inhibitor of class I and II HDACs, did not lead to significant changes in transcription, indicating that the repressive effect of H4K12su is not significantly mediated through HDAC1 in chromatinized templates assembled with non-acetylated histones (Schultz et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and citation to Schultz et al., 2004.

claim: The repressive effect of H4K12su is not significantly mediated through HDAC1 in chromatinized templates assembled with non-acetylated histones.
source: The addition of trichostatin A, a nanomolar inhibitor of class I and II HDACs, did not lead to significant changes in transcription, indicating that the repressive effect of H4K12su is not significantly mediated through HDAC1 in chromatinized templates assembled with non-acetylated histones (Schultz et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental observations.

claim: Site-specifically sumoylated H4 directly inhibits RNAPII-mediated transcription from chromatin templates.
source: Importantly, our results unambiguously demonstrated transcriptional repression when site-specifically sumoylated H4 was present in chromatin.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from in vitro transcription assays.

claim: Chromatinized plasmids containing either K-to-R mutations in the H4 tail or truncated H4 missing tail residues 1–19 revealed an ~80% reduced transcriptional output relative to transcription from chromatin containing wt H4.
source: Previous in vitro transcription studies with chromatinized plasmids containing either K-to-R mutations in the H4 tail or truncated H4 missing tail residues 1–19 revealed an ~80% reduced transcriptional output relative to transcription from chromatin containing wt H4 (An et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to An et al., 2002.

claim: The most abundant H4(4–17) peptide from wt H4 chromatin after p300 acetylation corresponded to the K5,8,12,16 tetra-acetylated form.
source: Analysis of the H4(4–17) tryptic peptides arising from wt H4 revealed a remarkable degree of hyperacetylation within 30 min. The most abundant peptide corresponded to the K5,8,12,16 tetra-acetylated form with some tri-acetylated species also present (Figure 3—source data 1, Figure 3A, Table 1, and Figure 3—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3A and Table 1.

claim: Chromatin assembled with H4K12su generated significantly fewer hyperacetylated peptides, with approximately equal amounts of tri- and di-acetylated H4(4–17) peptides.
source: In comparison, chromatin assembled with H4K12su generated significantly fewer hyperacetylated peptides, with approximately equal amounts of tri- and di-acetylated H4(4–17) peptides (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplements 5 and 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: H4K12su directly inhibits p300-mediated H4 tail acetylation in the steps prior to transcription.
source: This clearly indicates that H4K12su directly inhibits p300-mediated H4 tail acetylation in the steps prior to transcription.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the mass spectrometry data.

claim: H4K12su may inhibit transcription, in part, by directly inhibiting p300 activity on H4.
source: Given the importance of H4 tail acetylation for efficient transcription, H4K12su may inhibit transcription, in part, by directly inhibiting p300 activity on H4.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental observations.

claim: K5 and K8 are preferred sites in the double acetylated H4 tail by p300, over acetylation at K12 and K16.
source: Consistent with previous reports, we observed that K5 and K8 are preferred sites in the double acetylated H4 tail, over acetylation at K12 and K16 (Table 2; Schiltz et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Table 2 and citation to Schiltz et al., 1999.

claim: K12 was preferentially acetylated over K16 in the triply acetylated H4 tail peptide by p300.
source: Additionally, K12 was preferentially acetylated over K16 in the triply acetylated H4 tail peptide (Table 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Table 3.

claim: The intrinsic substrate preference of p300 is unchanged in the presence of SUMO-3.
source: These observations were consistent between H4 or H4K12su containing substrates, indicating that the intrinsic substrate preference of p300 is unchanged in the presence of SUMO-3 (Table 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Table 4.

claim: The attachment of SUMO-3 to the N-terminus of H4 significantly inhibits H4K16ac in HEK293T cells.
source: This analysis revealed that the attachment of SUMO-3 to the N-terminus of H4 significantly inhibits H4K16ac and has a smaller inhibitory effect on H4K12ac (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The attachment of SUMO-3 to the N-terminus of H4 has a smaller inhibitory effect on H4K12ac in HEK293T cells.
source: This analysis revealed that the attachment of SUMO-3 to the N-terminus of H4 significantly inhibits H4K16ac and has a smaller inhibitory effect on H4K12ac (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The ectopically expressed HA-Su3(ΔGG)-H4 fusion was incorporated into chromatin within human cells.
source: The presence of all core histones in the pulldown also demonstrated that the ectopically expressed HA-Su3(ΔGG)-H4 fusion was incorporated into chromatin within human cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The biochemical relationship observed in HEK293T cells is consistent with the observation that H4K12su inhibits H4K16ac in vitro.
source: Thus, the biochemical relationship observed in HEK293T cells is consistent with our observation that H4K12su inhibits H4K16ac in vitro, and further indicates a degree of plasticity in the precise site of sumoylation that may exhibit negative biochemical crosstalk with H4K16ac.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental observations.

claim: There is a degree of plasticity in the precise site of sumoylation that may exhibit negative biochemical crosstalk with H4K16ac.
source: Thus, the biochemical relationship observed in HEK293T cells is consistent with our observation that H4K12su inhibits H4K16ac in vitro, and further indicates a degree of plasticity in the precise site of sumoylation that may exhibit negative biochemical crosstalk with H4K16ac.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental observations.

claim: H4 tail sumoylation inhibits p300 activity and other known H4K16 acetyltransferases such as hMOF and CBP.
source: These cellular studies also expand our discovery that H4 tail sumoylation inhibits p300 activity to include other known H4K16 acetyltransferases such as hMOF (Taipale et al., 2005) and CBP (Bannister and Kouzarides, 1996).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental observations and citations to prior literature.

claim: H3K4me3 is a key mark associated with active gene transcription.
source: Along with H4K16ac, trimethylation at Lys 4 in histone H3 (H3K4me3) is a key mark associated with active gene transcription (Santos-Rosa et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Santos-Rosa et al., 2002.

claim: H3K4me3 is installed by the SETD1A/B and MLL-1/2 enzyme complexes in humans.
source: In humans, H3K4me3 is installed by the SETD1A/B and MLL-1/2 enzyme complexes, while the corresponding yeast enzyme complex is COMPASS (Shilatifard, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Shilatifard, 2012.

claim: The corresponding yeast enzyme complex for H3K4me3 installation is COMPASS.
source: In humans, H3K4me3 is installed by the SETD1A/B and MLL-1/2 enzyme complexes, while the corresponding yeast enzyme complex is COMPASS (Shilatifard, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Shilatifard, 2012.

claim: The catalytic module that imparts enzymatic activity and product specificity is evolutionarily conserved in animals and yeast.
source: Importantly, the catalytic module (CM) that imparts enzymatic activity and product specificity is evolutionarily conserved in animals and yeast, and consists of Set1 and the subunits Swd1, Bre2, Swd3, and Sdc1 in COMPASS.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge in the field.

claim: The catalytic module of COMPASS consists of Set1 and the subunits Swd1, Bre2, Swd3, and Sdc1.
source: Importantly, the catalytic module (CM) that imparts enzymatic activity and product specificity is evolutionarily conserved in animals and yeast, and consists of Set1 and the subunits Swd1, Bre2, Swd3, and Sdc1 in COMPASS.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge in the field.

claim: Ubiquitylation at H2BK120 stimulates the methyltransferase activity of the eCM.
source: Although ubiquitylation at H2BK120 stimulates the methyltransferase activity of the eCM, it is not absolutely critical for nucleosome methylation by SET1/COMPASS complexes in vitro (Tang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tang et al., 2013.

claim: Ubiquitylation at H2BK120 is not absolutely critical for nucleosome methylation by SET1/COMPASS complexes in vitro.
source: Although ubiquitylation at H2BK120 stimulates the methyltransferase activity of the eCM, it is not absolutely critical for nucleosome methylation by SET1/COMPASS complexes in vitro (Tang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tang et al., 2013.

claim: H4K12su biochemically opposes the presence of H3K4me2 in nucleosomes by stimulating the activity of the H3K4me1/2 demethylase LSD1.
source: Based on our previous observation that H4K12su biochemically opposes the presence of H3K4me2 in nucleosomes by stimulating the activity of the H3K4me1/2 demethylase LSD1 (Dhall et al., 2017), we asked if H4K12su also directly opposes the installation of H3K4me3 in nucleosomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dhall et al., 2017.

claim: H4K12su inhibits the installation of H3K4me1/2/3 on nucleosomes by the COMPASS eCM.
source: These experiments clearly showed that H4K12su inhibits the installation of H3K4me1/2/3 on nucleosomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from methylation assays.

claim: The negative biochemical crosstalk between H4K12su and H3K4 methylation arises from the presence of the Spp1 subunit in the eCM.
source: Moreover, the negative biochemical crosstalk arises from the presence of the Spp1 subunit in the eCM, because the core five-protein CM (Set1, Swd1, Bre2, Swd3, Sdc1) remained active on nucleosomes with or without the presence of H4K12su (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The core five-protein CM (Set1, Swd1, Bre2, Swd3, Sdc1) remained active on nucleosomes with or without the presence of H4K12su.
source: Moreover, the negative biochemical crosstalk arises from the presence of the Spp1 subunit in the eCM, because the core five-protein CM (Set1, Swd1, Bre2, Swd3, Sdc1) remained active on nucleosomes with or without the presence of H4K12su (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: H4K12su in nucleosomes engages in negative biochemical crosstalk with p300-mediated acetylation within the same H4 tail, in cis.
source: Thus, we conclude that H4K12su in nucleosomes engages in negative biochemical crosstalk with p300-mediated acetylation within the same H4 tail, in cis, and may engage in negative biochemical crosstalk with the COMPASS-mediated methylation in the H3 tail, in trans.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental observations.

claim: H4K12su may engage in negative biochemical crosstalk with the COMPASS-mediated methylation in the H3 tail, in trans.
source: Thus, we conclude that H4K12su in nucleosomes engages in negative biochemical crosstalk with p300-mediated acetylation within the same H4 tail, in cis, and may engage in negative biochemical crosstalk with the COMPASS-mediated methylation in the H3 tail, in trans.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental observations.

claim: No significant effect on the level of H3K4 trimethylation was observed in nucleosomes containing HA-Su3(ΔGG)-H4 relative to total chromatin in the HEK293 chromatin input.
source: Interestingly, we observed no significant effect on the level of H3K4 trimethylation associated with nucleosomes containing HA-Su3(ΔGG)-H4 relative to total chromatin in the HEK293 chromatin input (Figure 6A and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Sumoylated H4 does not inhibit all H3K4 methyltransferases in humans.
source: This result clearly indicated that sumoylated H4 does not inhibit all H3K4 methyltransferases in humans.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental observations.

claim: Set1/COMPASS is the only H3K4 methyltransferase in yeast.
source: Although Set1/COMPASS is the only H3K4 methyltransferase in yeast, humans have the SETD1A/B and MLL1-4 family of enzymes.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge in the field.

claim: Humans have the SETD1A/B and MLL1-4 family of H3K4 methyltransferase enzymes.
source: Although Set1/COMPASS is the only H3K4 methyltransferase in yeast, humans have the SETD1A/B and MLL1-4 family of enzymes.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge in the field.

claim: The MLL family methyltransferases do not contain analogs of the COMPASS Spp1 subunit.
source: The MLL family methyltransferases do not contain analogs of the COMPASS Spp1 subunit that may enforce negative crosstalk with H4 (Figure 5B; Xue et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Xue et al., 2019.

claim: The human SETD1A/B complex has an analog of the Spp1 subunit, namely CXXC-type zinc finger protein 1 (CFP1).
source: However, the human SETD1A/B complex has an analog of the Spp1 subunit, namely CXXC-type zinc finger protein 1 (CFP1), which targets SET1 to actively transcribe gene promoters (Brown et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Brown et al., 2017.

claim: CFP1 targets SET1 to actively transcribe gene promoters.
source: However, the human SETD1A/B complex has an analog of the Spp1 subunit, namely CXXC-type zinc finger protein 1 (CFP1), which targets SET1 to actively transcribe gene promoters (Brown et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Brown et al., 2017.

claim: The addition of doxycycline led to the expression and incorporation of epitope-tagged FLAG-HA-Su3(ΔGG)-H4(Δ1–11) in chromatin as early as 4 hr post-induction.
source: The addition of doxycycline led to the expression and incorporation of epitope-tagged FLAG-HA-Su3(ΔGG)-H4(Δ1–11) in chromatin as early as 4 hr post-induction (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: There is a striking inverse correlation in the genomic localization of FLAG-HA-Su3(ΔGG)-H4(Δ1–11) and H3K4me3.
source: Our analysis of chromatinized DNA associated with FLAG-HA-Su3(ΔGG)-H4(Δ1–11) and H3K4me3 revealed a striking inverse correlation in their genomic localization (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: H3K4me3 was strongly accumulated at TSSs.
source: Although H3K4me3 was strongly accumulated at TSSs, FLAG-HA-Su3(ΔGG)-H4(Δ1–11) was diminished at TSSs and enriched at transcription end sites.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data.

claim: FLAG-HA-Su3(ΔGG)-H4(Δ1–11) was diminished at TSSs and enriched at transcription end sites.
source: Although H3K4me3 was strongly accumulated at TSSs, FLAG-HA-Su3(ΔGG)-H4(Δ1–11) was diminished at TSSs and enriched at transcription end sites.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data.

claim: ChIP-seq analysis of gene occupancy reiterated the biochemical crosstalk between H4 sumoylation and H3K4me3.
source: Thus, ChIP-seq analysis of gene occupancy reiterated the biochemical crosstalk between H4 sumoylation and H3K4me3.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the ChIP-seq data.

claim: Sumoylated histone H4 does not directly enable heterochromatin formation.
source: These studies suggested that sumoylated H4 does not directly enable heterochromatin formation and may instead act by recruiting LSD1 to genes.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from prior studies.

claim: Sumoylated H4 may act by recruiting LSD1 to genes.

claim: The simplest explanation for inhibition of H4 tail acetylation by H4K12su is that steric bulk of the 93-amino acid SUMO-3 at K12 prevents acetylation at proximal lysines.
source: While the simplest explanation is that steric bulk of the 93-amino acid SUMO-3 at K12 prevents acetylation at proximal lysines, this should not be taken for granted as ubiquitin-family modifications at lysines do not always occlude enzymatic activity at proximal sites.
evidence: This claim is based on speculation and inference.

claim: Ubiquitin-family modifications at lysines do not always occlude enzymatic activity at proximal sites.
source: While the simplest explanation is that steric bulk of the 93-amino acid SUMO-3 at K12 prevents acetylation at proximal lysines, this should not be taken for granted as ubiquitin-family modifications at lysines do not always occlude enzymatic activity at proximal sites.

claim: Ubiquitylation at K119 in the H2A C-terminus by PRC1 E3 ligases Ring1B/Bmi1 does not inhibit ubiquitylation at K124/K127/K129 in the H2A tail by the BRCA1-BARD1 heterodimeric E3 ligase.
source: For example, the ubiquitylation at K119 in the H2A C-terminus by the polycomb repressive complex 1 (PRC1) E3 ligases Ring1B/Bmi1 does not inhibit ubiquitylation at K124/K127/K129 in the H2A tail by the BRCA1-BARD1 heterodimeric E3 ligase (Uckelmann et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Uckelmann et al., 2018.

claim: Reduced acetylation may arise from a specific spatial orientation of the H4 tail upon its sumoylation that limits access to the p300 active site.
source: Reduced acetylation may equally arise from a specific spatial orientation of the H4 tail upon its sumoylation that limits access to the p300 active site.
evidence: This claim is based on speculation.

claim: Chromatinized plasmids containing H2B ubiquitylated at K120 show similar levels of transcription to unmodified chromatin.
source: As chromatinized plasmids containing H2B ubiquitylated at K120 show similar levels of transcription to unmodified chromatin (Kim et al., 2009), the inhibition of transcription we observed may not strictly be due to the steric bulk of SUMO in chromatin.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Kim et al., 2009.

claim: The inhibition of transcription by H4K12su may not strictly be due to the steric bulk of SUMO in chromatin.
source: As chromatinized plasmids containing H2B ubiquitylated at K120 show similar levels of transcription to unmodified chromatin (Kim et al., 2009), the inhibition of transcription we observed may not strictly be due to the steric bulk of SUMO in chromatin.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental observations and citation.

source: Interestingly, endogenous wt H4 in HA-tagged asymmetric mononucleosomes was also deficient in H4K16ac, when compared with H4K16ac in bulk chromatin.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations.

claim: There may be an additional trans-nucleosome mechanism of acetyltransferase inhibition by SUMO, in addition to its cis-inhibitory effect in the H4 tail.
source: This may indicate an additional trans-nucleosome mechanism of acetyltransferase inhibition by SUMO, in addition to its cis-inhibitory effect in the H4 tail.
evidence: This claim is based on speculation from the experimental observations.

claim: H3K4me3 activates p53- and p300-dependent transcription from chromatinized plasmids.
source: Installed by the Set1 containing COMPASS complex in yeast and the SET1/MLL1-2 family of methyltransferases in humans, H3K4me3 activates p53- and p300-dependent transcription from chromatinized plasmids (Tang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tang et al., 2013.

claim: SUMO may sterically interact with the Spp1 subunit in the eCM and may reduce nucleosome binding and/or productive catalysis by the Set1 protein.
source: From the differences in composition of the two sub-complexes, we propose that SUMO may sterically interact with the Spp1 subunit in the eCM and may reduce nucleosome binding and/or productive catalysis by the Set1 protein.
evidence: This claim is based on speculation and inference from the experimental observations.

claim: SUMO attached to the H4 tail may reside on a specific surface of the nucleosome that prevents the close apposition of adjacent nucleosomes and the binding of histone-modifying enzymes.
source: Our results from methyltransferase assays, in conjunction with previous observations that H4 tail sumoylation inhibits chromatin compaction, appear to indicate that SUMO attached to the H4 tail does not extend away from the nucleosome, but instead may reside on a specific surface of the nucleosome that prevents the close apposition of adjacent nucleosomes and the binding of histone-modifying enzymes .
evidence: This claim is based on speculation and inference from the experimental observations.

claim: Histone acetylation by p300 stimulates SETD1 activity on chromatin.
source: As histone acetylation by p300 also stimulates SETD1 activity on chromatin, the direct effect of H4K12su on p300-stimulated SETD1 methylation at H3K4 also remains an interesting question (Tang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tang et al., 2013.

claim: The direct effect of H4K12su on p300-stimulated SETD1 methylation at H3K4 remains an interesting question.
source: As histone acetylation by p300 also stimulates SETD1 activity on chromatin, the direct effect of H4K12su on p300-stimulated SETD1 methylation at H3K4 also remains an interesting question (Tang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is based on speculation about future research directions.

claim: H4K12su does not inhibit H3K4 methylation genome-wide, but may specifically inhibit the methylation of transcriptionally active genes by the SETD1A/B complexes.
source: Thus, our extensive investigations of biochemical crosstalk revealed that H4K12su does not inhibit H3K4 methylation genome-wide, but, instead may specifically inhibit the methylation of transcriptionally active genes by the SETD1A/B complexes.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental observations.

claim: The disruption of H4 tail acetylation and H3 tail methylation by H4K12su, along with the inhibition of p300-mediated transcription from chromatinized templates, have revealed multiple biochemical pathways by which histone sumoylation may inhibit gene transcription.
source: Collectively, the disruption of H4 tail acetylation and H3 tail methylation by the presence of H4K12su along with the inhibition of p300-mediated transcription from chromatinized templates have revealed multiple, albeit not exhaustive, biochemical pathways by which histone sumoylation may inhibit gene transcription (Figure 7).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental observations shown in Figure 7.
